channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

Nature Communications: CCR8-depleting antibodies restore response to radiotherapy plus anti-PD1 therapy in head and neck cancer by targeting intratumoral CCR8+ regulatory T cells
item.description: Previous evidence has implicated regulatory T cells (Tregs) in treatment resistance in head and neck cancer. Here the authors report that radiotherapy and anti-PD1 therapy drive the accumulation and activation of intratumoral CCR8+ Tregs, promoting tumor growth and recurrence, which can be reversed with administration of CCR8 depleting antibodies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Failure of TSPO-dependent metabolic compensation marks the loss of mitochondrial bioenergetic adaptation in parkin- deficient neurons
item.description: Neurons initially adapt to mitochondrial damage, but why this defence fails is unclear. Here, the authors show that TSPO maintains glutamate-supported mitochondrial energy production in parkin-deficient neurons, and loss of this defence marks the transition from adaptation to neurodegeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: LRH-1 coordinates metabolic and epigenetic programs that establish luteal cell identity
item.description: Gagnon et al. show that LRH-1 coordinates metabolic and epigenetic programs that establish large luteal cell identity, progesterone production and fertility.

item.title: Nature Communications: Directional motility of crystallizing cholesterol on supported lipid bilayers
item.description: Cholesterol crystallizing inside a lipid membrane reshapes the membrane around it. Here, authors show that cholesterol crystallites travel in directed paths across model membranes, and map how lipid composition tunes that motion.

item.title: Nature Communications: A hierarchical metabolic flux orchestrates cell cycle transitions in bacteria
item.description: How cells coordinate growth and division with their metabolic state is poorly understood. Here, Agrawal et al. describe changes in glucose uptake and central metabolism that alter cytosolic redox balance and drive cell cycle progression in the bacterial model Caulobacter crescentus .

item.title: Nature Communications: miProbe: microbial peptide repository of biological embeddings
item.description: Authors present miProbe, a platform aimed to consolidate peptide data and functional characterisation, and presenting a resource to accelerate AI-driven exploration of microbial dark matter.

item.title: Nature Communications: Comparative genomics analysis of luminescent and non-luminescent fireflies reveals mechanisms underlying adult light organs development
item.description: Not all fireflies emit light. Here they perform comparative genomics between luminous and non-luminous fireflies to reveal that light organ loss stems from simplified gene networks. They show that Laccase2 is essential for light organ integrity, offering insights into bioluminescence trait evolution.

item.title: Nature Communications: A microfluidic fluorescence lifetime screening platform bridges in vitro and in vivo formats and enables discovery of Amyloid β aggregation inhibitors
item.description: Alzheimer’s drug discovery is hindered by unreliable tests for Amyloid β aggregation. Here, the authors develop nanoFLIM, a microfluidic screening tool to identify and validate aggregation inhibitors in vitro, in cellulo and in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
item.description: Two-photon oblique plane microscopy combines high-numerical-aperture single-objective detection with two-photon light-sheet illumination, resolving subcellular and single-molecule dynamics deep in multicellular systems through standard glass-based mounting.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
item.description: The role of peripheral signals in sleep state regulation is not well understood. Here authors show that vagal sensory afferent activation induces a NREMS-like state with low-frequency EEG, slowed heart rate, and cooling, while elevating locus coeruleus noradrenergic activity, revealing brain arousal within a sleep-like state.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sex differences in the genetic basis of human recombination within 190,000 parent-child pairs
item.description: A meta-analysis of 190,797 human meioses across four countries maps 24 recombination loci, seven novel and mostly female-specific. Between-sex genetic correlation is 0.37, and a polygenic predictor links female recombination to reproduction and aging.

item.title: Nature Communications: The posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell circuit mediates an anti-pruritic response
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying itch are not fully understood. Here authors show that the pPVT-NAcMed (posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell) circuit oppositely responds to histamine-dependent vs -independent itch, with LH inputs buffering the former, but chronic itch reduces postsynaptic efficacy, promoting sensitization and revealing differential processing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Epithelium stratifies via nucleation and growth induced by foam-geometric instability
item.description: Researchers show that epithelial stratification, the shift from monolayer to multilayers, occurs via a nucleation-and-growth process. Combining cell cultures and 3D modeling, this study reveals how local cell delaminations drive tissue-wide changes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intrinsic neural dynamics reveal a body-part-specific topography in mouse secondary motor cortex
item.description: This presents a body-part-specific topography in mouse secondary motor cortex by analyzing intrinsic brain dynamics. The map is structurally and functionally linked to homologous sensory regions, and is selectively engaged during multi-part actions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
item.description: In this clinical trial, authors found that administering the COVID-19 antibody AZD7442 before vaccination was safe in immunocompromised adults and boosted immune responses. The findings support combining antibodies and vaccines to protect vulnerable people.

item.title: Nature Communications: AS01 E -adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial
item.description: The authors report results from a randomized phase 2 trial showing that the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine was immunogenic and had an acceptable safety profile in lung and kidney transplant recipients, supporting a favorable benefit-risk profile.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life and biological aging and age-related diseases
item.description: Exposure to sugar rationing during the first 1,000 days of life was associated with slower biological aging in adulthood, with stronger associations after longer exposure. It was also associated with lower risks of several age-related diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Post-pandemic immunity debt and environmental decoupling reshape urban influenza transmission
item.description: Using 1.88 million clinical records from Macau and regional and global surveillance, in this study, the authors show how reduced population immunity and renewed travel reshaped post-pandemic influenza transmission and weakened its usual links with climate.

item.title: Nature Communications: ISG15 promotes PARP inhibitor resistance in BRCA1-deficient cells by facilitating DNA replication and repair
item.description: Despite promising initial responses, BRCA1/2 -mutated cancers treated with PARP inhibitors (PARPi) often develop resistance. Here, the authors show that PARPi-resistant BRCA1-deficient models lose TP53BP1 expression and upregulate factors of the ISGylation machinery, including ISG15, which supports replication fork progression/restart and facilitates homologous recombination-mediated DNA repair, driving PARPi resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: scMomer: a pretraining framework for inferring robust cellular representations from single-cell transcriptomes
item.description: Here, the authors develop scMomer, a pretraining framework that infers multimodal-aware cellular representations from scRNA-seq data alone. By distilling chromatin accessibility knowledge, the authors show that this method can be applied to different downstream single-cell tasks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of ligand-mediated transition to higher-order rubisco assemblies
item.description: Proteins often assemble into complexes, and while binding partners typically drive this, ligand binding can too. Here the authors show ligand binding drives distinct rubisco assemblies, revealing an evolutionary path to greater structural complexity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
item.description: In this study, the authors use comparative genomics and cross-infection assays to show a spatially and evolutionarily structured bacterial immune reservoir in which interactions among defense systems can reinforce or undermine phage resistance, refining the pan-immunity framework.

item.title: Nature Communications: A single NLS directs AGO1 import shaping small RNA loading and silencing outputs in Arabidopsis
item.description: Small RNAs guide ARGONAUTE proteins to their targets. Here the authors identify a pathway controlling AGO1 nuclear import and show that AGO1 subcellular localization shapes small RNA loading and silencing outputs in plants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Latitude modulates climate-driven maize yield gains across the central U.S. “warming hole”
item.description: Climate change affects crop yield variation across regions and seasons. This study suggests that climate impacts on maize yields shift from losses in the southern U.S. Corn Belt to gains in the north, driven by climate trends, thermal matching, and hybrid selection.

item.title: Nature Communications: A prefrontal microcircuit computes trial-wise discount of reinforcement during threat learning in male mice
item.description: Neural mechanisms underlying threat learning are not fully understood. Here authors identify a prefrontal circuit that constrains early threat learning in male mice. Local inhibitory neurons may release this constraint, providing a mechanism for regulating how strongly each experience shapes memory.

item.title: Nature Communications: Engineering CAR-Vδ2 T cells to boost persistence and anti-tumor function
item.description: CAR-Vδ2 T cells show promise for cancer immunotherapy, but their efficacy is limited by poor persistence and activation induced cell death. Here, this group propose an engineered CAR-Vδ2 T design that leverages IL18 signaling inducing a durable expansion in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extinction risks in deep-sea populations revealed by genomic data and ecological niche modeling
item.description: Here authors use genomic data to reveal indicators of elevated extinction risk in Gulf of Mexico mesopelagic species. Together with projected declines in habitat suitability, these findings raise the possibility of a broader, unnoticed crisis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Epigenetic gatekeeping enables genome-scale horizontal gene transfer in eukaryotic cells
item.description: Aoki et al . show that mammalian cells can acquire and retain chromosome-scale DNA from algae. The study reveals that host DNA methylation helps establish and maintain foreign DNA, offering insight into gene transfer between distant species.

item.title: Nature Communications: SIP-enabled multi-omics reveals soil microbiome responses to drought and rehydration
item.description: This study demonstrates that soil microbial growth rates are extremely slow under dry conditions, with rehydration causing a rapid increase in anabolic activity within days. These findings refine our understanding of microbial contributions to soil carbon cycling with a warming climate.

item.title: Nature Communications: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
item.description: Researchers developed UniRG, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes clinically aligned composite rewards for medical imaging report generation. UniRG outperforms prior models and demonstrates strong generalization across unseen hospitals and datasets

Nature Communications: Nudix protein D250R promotes African swine fever virus infection by disrupting host ubiquitination machinery
item.description: This study uncovers a novel African swine fever virus (ASFV) immune-evasion mechanism targeting ubiquitin activation and identifies D250R as a key virulence factor. Loss of D250R attenuates the virus and supports its potential as a live attenuated vaccine candidate against ASF.

item.title: Nature Communications: UMIche: a UMI-centric analysis platform for enhancing molecular quantification accuracy in bulk and single-cell sequencing
item.description: Errors in unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) can distort molecule counts. Here, the authors present UMIche, a platform for benchmarking deduplication methods, and show that set cover and majority voting are more robust as barcode errors increase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pigment repression protects fungus from ferroptosis to maintain virulence
item.description: The phytopathogenic fungus Fusarium graminearum produces a secondary metabolite, aurofusarin, at late stages during wheat infection. Here, the authors show how the biosynthesis of aurofusarin is regulated to avoid host-induced iron stress that results from the formation of iron complexes by an aurofusarin intermediate.

item.title: Nature Communications: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity
item.description: OsPUB2 degrades OsPUB12 to promote rice immunity. Phosphorylation of OsPUB12 by OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 at two sites fine-tunes its stability and the plant’s defense response.

item.title: Nature Communications: Functionally divergent RHOA mutations drive peripheral T cell lymphoma development by engaging a common neomorphic pathway
item.description: RHOA mutation variants, exerting opposite effects on canonical RHOA signaling, are associated with peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCL). Here, the authors show that different RHOA mutants share a neomorphic activity that activates the transcription factor NFAT to drive PTCL.

item.title: Nature Communications: ATR promotes genome instability via CENP-A eviction from centromeres after prolonged exposure to genotoxic stress
item.description: Interphase DNA damage can lead to genome instability by promoting missegregation of chromosomes lacking centromeres. Here the authors show that DNA damage activates ATR and driving VCP-dependent eviction of CENP-A from centromeres to nucleoli. CENP-A loss causes increased chromosomes missegregation, linking DNA damage to centromere dysfunction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression
item.description: Rafeh et al. use frequency-tagged fMRI to demonstrate that selective attention relies on dual, independent neural mechanisms for target enhancement and surround suppression, elaborating on traditional unitary models of human visual attention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Experience modifies the synaptome architecture in the developing and adult mouse brain
item.description: The effect of experiences on brain-wide synapse populations is unknown. Here, the authors show that environment and visual input drive changes in excitatory synapse types and subtypes across the mouse brain during development and adulthood.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pharmacological chaperone treatment with Cystadane in aspartylglucosaminuria: an open-label, phase Ib/II trial
item.description: Here, this phase Ib/II interventional clinical trial shows that betaine/Cystadane is safe to use and significantly reduces urinary accumulation of glycoasparagines and increases aspartylglucosaminidase activity in aspartylglucosaminuria.

item.title: Nature Communications: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
item.description: Skin-attached devices can easily inflame or collapse. Here, the authors show a multi-lobed microneedle device that holds micron-scale conduits open for seven days, allowing repeated protein sampling from interstitial fluid

item.title: Nature Communications: Cryo-EM reveals conserved baseplate-architecture and distinct accessory-protein assemblies in mycobacteriophages Claus, Corndog and Mysterious
item.description: Atomic-resolution structures of three mycobacteriophages reveal a conserved baseplate core decorated by diverse accessory proteins, showing how related siphophages build distinct baseplate architectures from a common structural core.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
item.description: In this study, the authors analyze over 30,000 assembled metagenomes across ecosystems to uncover hidden protist diversity, including major novel uncultivated lineages, and reveal their habitats and connections to other microbes.

item.title: Nature Communications: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
item.description: In this study, the authors use metagenomics to map the diverse and previously unknown bacteria responsible for taking up methane across Denmark’s varied environments and highlight the natural habitats and methanotroph species with the potential for methane mitigation.

item.title: Nature Communications: A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
item.description: Bone metastases in advanced prostate cancer remain difficult to treat and are associated with poor outcomes. Here, the authors show that bone-colonizing prostate tumor cells exploit lactate uptake via MCT1 to fuel tumor growth and promote osteogenesis, identifying MCT1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Nature Communications: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
item.description: The brain organizes relationships between entities into cognitive maps. Here, the authors show that complementary stable and context-dependent representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, with their geometry shaped by cognitive control.

item.title: Nature Communications: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
item.description: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder causes cyclical mental symptoms, but how these symptoms unfold over time is not yet understood. This study reveals temporal patterns and identifies anxiety as a promising treatment target.

item.title: Nature Communications: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
item.description: Role of specific immune and inflammation-related pathways and protein markers in the development of prostate cancer remains to be elucidated. Here the authors show evidence for potential protective role of dendritic cell mediated immunosurveillance, with protective associations with immune and inflammation related proteins measured more than seven years before diagnosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
item.description: A study of 51 patients receiving deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression shows that individual white matter stimulation and integrity jointly influence antidepressant response, supporting more personalized neuromodulation strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: The transcriptional regulator IκBζ is essential for ILC2 effector functions
item.description: Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2) are important for the anti-helminth immune response. Here the authors show that the effector program of ILC2s depends on transcriptional regulation of the alarmins IL-25 and IL-33 by IκBζ, leading to efficient hookworm clearance in a mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nanometer-resolution imaging of living bacteria across species and cellular orientations
item.description: The use of atomic force microscopy for high-resolution imaging of the surface of live bacterial cells is limited by challenges in cell immobilization. Here, Scheeder et al. present an improved immobilization method that allows imaging of diverse bacteria, including imaging of bacterial cell poles.

item.title: Nature Communications: Calpain-mediated TBP cleavage disturbs neuronal AMOT-YAP1 signalling
item.description: TBP fragments activate calpains and disrupt AMOT-YAP1 signalling, revealing a pathway involved in normal neural development and implicated in spinocerebellar ataxia type 17.

item.title: Nature Communications: Electrode-associated growth reveals structure of OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires in anaerobic methanotrophic archaea
item.description: Anaerobic methanotrophic archaea are key regulators of methane emissions in anoxic environments. Here, the authors report near-axenic cultivation of these microorganisms on electrodes, describing key physiological traits and presence of OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires likely involved in extracellular electron transfer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Two functionally distinct amyloid-β intermediates link aggregation pathways to pathology in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Authors combine super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule functional imaging with kinetic modelling to classify Aβ intermediates according to their membrane-disrupting activity and connect their damaging effects to the aggregation pathways that generate them, connecting model systems with human pathology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell machine learning uncovers genetically anchored, cell-type specific programs of Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Univariate analyses alone cannot resolve multivariate disease-associated structure. Here, the authors develop TriSCOPE, a machine learning approach that identifies gene programs specific to individual brain cell types in Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Absolute quantification and profiling of cellular tRNAs by nanopore sequencing and a deep learning classifier
item.description: Here the authors develop a nanopore-based method using deep learning to classify cellular tRNAs, quantify their absolute abundance, and detect chemical modifications at the single molecule level.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hydration water drives elastin’s entropic elasticity
item.description: Elastin endows biological tissues with their remarkable elasticity, yet the molecular basis of its recoil has long remained unresolved. By simulating a representative elastomeric region of monomeric tropoelastin, and quantifying both protein conformational entropy and hydrationwater entropy, the authors provide an atomistic comparison of their respective contributions to elasticity. Their analysis reveals that hydration water is the dominant entropic driver of elastin recoil, acting within a finely balanced thermodynamic framework that governs stretch-induced molecular responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts future PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives with expert-level accuracy
item.description: PTSD screening is rarely feasible in busy emergency departments. Here, the authors show that a scalable AI ensemble can predict 1-month PTSD risk from a single routine-care question, a first step toward low-burden implementation at point of care.

item.title: Nature Communications: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
item.description: Second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa . Here, the authors show how the bacteria switch between attachment and surface movement by coordinating the two signalling systems, allowing distinct bacterial populations to work together to colonise and damage human airway tissue.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phosphorylation-driven targeted protein degradation of oncogenic β-catenin
item.description: Wolf et al. used proteome-scale induced-proximity screens for inhibitors of the oncogene β-catenin in colorectal cancer and discovered induced kinase-dependent degradation as an expansion of the Targeted Protein Degradation concept.

item.title: Nature Communications: WASH orchestrates phagosomal maturation and bacterial killing in neutrophils through syntaxin 19-mediated lysosomal fusion
item.description: How actin regulates late phagosomal maturation and microbial killing in neutrophils remains unclear. The authors here show that WASH drives actin-dependent lysosomal dynamics and STX19 recruitment to phagosomes, enabling lysosome fusion and bacterial killing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide CRISPR screening in Spodoptera frugiperda reveals the determinants of insecticide activation and sensitivity
item.description: New tools to investigate the molecular determinants of insect sensitivity to insecticides are needed. Here, a new genome-wide CRISPR-based screening platform is established and used to identify genes involved in activating the insecticide pyridalyl.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transposable element polymorphisms underlie epigenetic variation and phenotypic diversification during foxtail millet domestication
item.description: Foxtail millet is one of the oldest domesticated crops with climate-resilient trait and balanced nutrients. Here, the authors analyze methylome over a set of 60 foxtail millet accessions and reveal transposable element polymorphisms underlying epigenetic variation and phenotypic diversification during domestication.

item.title: Nature Communications: Retrospective single cell lineage tracing with highly mutable homopolymers
item.description: Cell lineage reconstruction can reveal developmental histories, but current methods are limited by marker density and accuracy. Here, the authors develop RETrace2, a dual‑omic single‑cell approach that combines highly mutable homopolymer markers with methylation profiling to enable high‑resolution lineage tracing and cell‑type identification.

item.title: Nature Communications: Propofol induces sustained suppression of alcohol drinking via habenular activation in mice
item.description: The lateral habenula is known to regulate alcohol drinking behaviors in mice. Here, the authors show that a single dose of propofol reduces voluntary alcohol drinking in mice via hyperactivity of neurons in the lateral habenula, and through propofol interaction with the 5-HT2C receptor.

item.title: Nature Communications: Insular motor and error encoding supports self-correcting intracranial brain-computer interface
item.description: Weger and colleagues demonstrate a brain-computer interface harnessing insular activity to detect errors and enable real-time correction, while characterizing the spatio-temporal progression of error signals from insular to prefrontal cortices.

item.title: Nature Communications: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
item.description: A soft robotic and computational framework replicates left atrial hemodynamics. Validated with human and porcine data, the platform enables personalized preclinical testing of left atrial appendage occlusion devices for atrial fibrillation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella evolved divergent human intestinal epithelial cell tropism
item.description: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause gastroenteritis and typhoid fever, respectively. Here, McKenna et al. show that the two types of serovars use opposing pre-invasion strategies to sense and invade human intestinal epithelium.

item.title: Nature Communications: Continuous directed evolution using engineered human B cell lines
item.description: This study describes the development of a continuous directed evolution platform in human B cell lines (CODE-HB) that repurposes the somatic hypermutation (SHM) mechanisms to evolve cytoplasmic reporter proteins as well as therapeutically relevant antibodies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan
item.description: How the bilaterian body plan originated from a cnidarian–bilaterian ancestor remains an intriguing evolutionary question. This study proposes a new scenario for how the chordate body plan could have evolved from this ancestor.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
item.description: Similar memories can be confused in different ways depending on how learning has progressed. This research shows the hippocampus responds by separating memories along the specific dimension of similarity, causing confusion at each stage of learning.

item.title: Nature Communications: Non-canonical FOXO1 signaling governs epithelial barrier integrity through spatial regulation of the E-cadherin–β-catenin complex
item.description: Bacterial challenge rapidly weakens epithelial barriers through a non-canonical, FOXO1–β-catenin–E-cadherin axis that disrupts adherens junctions and redistributes E-cadherin independently of transcription or proteolysis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Adipocyte enhancer binding protein 1 (AEBP1) inhibition mediates cardiac reverse remodeling by regulating MRTFB and RUNX2 signaling
item.description: Cardiac fibrosis contributes to adverse remodeling and heart failure progression, but its molecular drivers remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ACLP/AEBP1 promotes cardiac fibrosis and AEBP1 inhibition following injury, improves cardiac structure and function.

item.title: Nature Communications: A topographic video model predicts the spatio-functional organization of the human visual system
item.description: How the brain organizes dynamic visual processing remains unclear. Here the authors reorganize a video foundation model onto a simulated cortical sheet, reproducing face-, body- and motion-selective clusters embedded in smooth selectivity gradients.

item.title: Nature Communications: A 17.2T MRI atlas and multiparametric exploration of the mouse hypothalamus reveal sexual dimorphism and lateralization
item.description: This 17.2 Tesla MRI study provides a nucleus-level atlas of the mouse hypothalamus, mapping its anatomy, structural and functional connectivity, and neurochemical profile, revealing sex-related differences in structure and neurochemistry.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phospholipase D1 activates NAD kinase fuelling neutrophil extracellular trap formation
item.description: Neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation is a key innate response that relies on NADPH oxidase-driven production of reactive oxygen species. Here, the authors implicate phospholipase D1 in the activation of NAD kinase linked to NET formation.

item.title: Nature Communications: [ 18 F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma
item.description: Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) is standard for patients with glioblastoma, but its ability to detect metabolically active tumours cells at the infiltrative edge is limited. Here, the authors present a prospective biopsy-validated study demonstrating that ¹⁸F-FET PET imaging can detect tumour tissue beyond that detected by CE-MRI in patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microbiome-derived proline dipeptides underpin improved nitrogen utilization efficiency in dairy cattle
item.description: Here, they find that rumen microbes produce proline-containing peptides that underpin more efficient nitrogen use in dairy cows, revealing microbial targets for more sustainable milk production.

item.title: Nature Communications: Estimating the resilience of non-stationary systems
item.description: The authors introduce a method applicable to diverse Earth system components that directly estimates recovery rates and robust uncertainty estimates and can accommodate data with uneven sampling, seasonality, and time-varying uncertainties.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial
item.description: It is unclear whether adjunct intra-arterial Tenecteplase during thrombectomy improves clinical outcomes in patients with acute large vessel occlusion. Here, the authors show that adjunct intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy does not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial
item.description: Medium-vessel occlusion accounts for a substantial proportion of acute ischemic stroke cases, yet optimal reperfusion treatment strategies remain unclear for patients ineligible for mechanical endovascular thrombectomy. Here, the authors show that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increases reperfusion rates for medium-vessel occlusion with acceptable safety, although statistically-significant improvements in 90-day functional outcomes were not detected in this phase-2 randomized trial.

item.title: Nature Communications: Redundancy maximization as a principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks
item.description: Local computational principles for modeling associative memory remain incompletely understood. The authors show that high local redundant information between the inputs of each neuron is a key principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks, and that direct maximization of this redundancy results in a new state-of-the-art learning rule.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial
item.description: Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is a life-threatening cause of stroke, and whether intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization leads to improved outcomes is unclear. This randomized trial by Chen and colleagues was stopped early for safety concerns and shows that adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase does not improve functional outcomes in acute BAO.

item.title: Nature Communications: A pilot randomized controlled trial of medically tailored groceries and resource coaching: secondary and exploratory diet and health outcomes
item.description: Here, the authors report secondary and exploratory outcomes of a pilot randomized controlled trial exploring a food-is-medicine intervention of medically tailored groceries with or without resource coaching against usual pantry support. All groups improved over time in food security, diet quality, and perceived health, but baseline-adjusted analyses did not identify clear differences between the groups.

item.title: Nature Communications: Engineering filamentous myosins for optical control of contractility
item.description: Zemsky and colleagues employ protein engineering to create filamentous myosins controlled by light. These optogenetic motors enable spatiotemporal control of contractility in vitro and in cells, providing a tool for probing contractile actomyosin systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
item.description: Predicting how mutations affect enzyme catalytic efficiency remains challenging. Here the authors build a benchmark dataset and develop DeltaCata, a geometric deep learning model that predicts changes in enzyme kinetics and guides enzyme engineering.

item.title: Nature Communications: The modular evolution of chitinases is governed by coevolution of auxiliary and catalytic domains
item.description: Changes in the arrangement of protein domains shape the evolution of chitin-degrading enzymes, helping bacteria and archaea specialize for different ecological niches.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genomic language models decode bidirectional promoter activity and reveal conserved regulatory patterns across plant species
item.description: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs) are intergenic regions that initiate transcription of two oppositely oriented genes. Here, the authors report a framework that employs Evo2 genomic language model embeddings to predict BDP activity directly from raw DNA sequence.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diacylglycerol Metabolism Drives Host–pathogen Responses During Enteric Infection in Drosophila
item.description: Li et al. reveal a lipid-dependent signaling axis that links intestinal epithelial cells and intestinal muscle to gut motility and bacterial pathogen clearance, offering mechanistic insight into how lipid dynamics orchestrate host defenses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chemokine and opioid peptide scavenging through constitutive and ligand-induced release of ACKR3-bearing extracellular vesicles
item.description: Ligand scavenging by ACKR3 is known to rely on intracellular uptake. Here, authors show that ACKR3 is also released on extracellular vesicles as a functional sequestrator of chemokines and opioid peptides, revealing another dimension of regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Energy-guided combinatorial co-optimization of antibody affinity and stability
item.description: Here, Tennenhouse et al. develop LAffAb, a structure-based method for designing CDR mutations to improve affinity and developability. By filtering mutations predicted to disrupt stability and foldability, LAffAb enables accurate, one-shot design.

item.title: Nature Communications: Resident cardiac macrophage-like cells induced by an ILC2 cytokine cocktail confer cardioprotection through enhanced efferocytosis in a mouse model of myocardial infarction
item.description: Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) contribute to cardiac repair after myocardial infarction (MI); however, their number is reduced upon injury. Here, the authors identify a population of efferocytosing CD301b+ macrophages that promote post-ischemic cardiac repair and develop an ex vivo protocol to generate RCM-like cells induced with enhanced efferocytic potential for post-MI cardioprotection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pathology-adapted peptide–oligonucleotide nanohybrid mitigates glucocorticoid-induced bone loss
item.description: Glucocorticoids can cause severe bone loss and osteonecrosis. Here, the authors develop a pathology-adapted peptide–oligonucleotide nanohybrid that delivers miR 26a-5p to mitigate bone loss and support vascular recovery.

item.title: Nature Communications: Two distinct α2β1 integrin glycan interactions mediate cell entry of a picornavirus
item.description: Equine rhinitis A virus (ERAV) causes respiratory infections in horses, yet its receptor for binding remained elusive. Using a combination of virological, genetic, structural, and glycoproteomic approaches, Owino et al. show that ERAV utilizes integrin α2β1 as a receptor in a cation-independent manner.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
item.description: Using fMRI, the authors show that numerosity-sensitive neural populations in human parietal cortex shift and rescale their tuning to match the range of numbers encountered. This neural flexibility supports behavioral adaptability.

item.title: Nature Communications: Disrupting the semantic network shifts activity to domain-general brain regions
item.description: Disrupting a key language region prompts increased activity in widespread brain regions. Stronger engagement of frontal control regions helps preserve cognitive performance, revealing the brain’s capacity to adapt to interference in real time.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiscale neural dynamics reveal how striatal subregions shape stress vulnerability and resilience
item.description: This study shows that striatal subregions shape individual differences in stress vulnerability and resilience through distinct patterns of multiscale network dynamics during stress coping.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell atlas uncovers layer 4 heterogeneity and functional gradients in rhesus macaque visual cortex
item.description: Macaques are pivotal models for decoding human visual processing, but there is a lack of area-specific data on their visual cortex. Here, authors show area-specific diversity in principal neurons along the visual processing hierarchy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mannitol-stimulated Copeptin for diagnosing Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency: a randomized controlled proof of concept and a single-arm pilot study
item.description: Distinguishing arginine vasopressin deficiency from primary polydipsia can be difficult and current tests are challenging. Here, the authors show that mannitol-stimulated copeptin may offer a simple, rapid, safe and accurate diagnostic alternative.

item.title: Nature Communications: Personalized adjunctive phage therapy for difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections
item.description: In this prospective study, authors found that personalized adjunctive local phage therapy was feasible and well tolerated in difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections, with 9 of 11 evaluable patients achieving remission.

item.title: Nature Communications: Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
item.description: Here they uncover an unexpectedly early role for Wt1 in biasing lineage programmes before gastrulation and show that Wt1 isoforms differing only by a three-amino-acid KTS motif encode divergent anterior-posterior lineage biases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) prevents excessive protein aggregation and mediates aggrephagy by modulating the liquidity of p62 condensates
item.description: VHL shows an unexpected HIF-independent role in maintaining protein homeostasis under proteotoxic stress, namely, by increasing the liquidity of p62 condensates and orchestrating aggresome formation and subsequent aggrephagy.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vitro–reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
item.description: Capsid-forming proteins are promising vehicles for macromolecule delivery, but have required cellular assembly or fusogens for entry. Here, authors assemble Drosophila Arc1 capsids cell-free, show entry via the receptor SORCS2, and deliver Cas9 editors that restore dystrophin in mdx mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Colonic enterochromaffin cells modulate a neuronal-immune-epithelial cell axis for antimicrobial homeostasis
item.description: In the gut, epithelial, neuronal, and immune cells collaborate to maintain microbiota homeostasis, but molecular insights are still lacking. Here the authors deplete epithelial enteroendocrine cells in mouse colons via Satb2-mediated Neurog3 deficiency to uncover a serotonin/CGRP/IL-13 axis of antimicrobial peptide regulation that is validated in organoid cultures.

item.title: Nature Communications: PRMT6 suppresses intestinal inflammation by epigenetically repressing IL-1β in mouse models of colitis
item.description: Epigenetic regulation in immune cells drive their physiological and pathologic development, including establishment of inflammatory states. Here the authors show in mouse colitis models, that genomic deletion of the protein arginine methyltransferase PRMT6 leads to a selective upregulation of IL-1β in macrophages and to exacerbated inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Alpha-aminoadipate in the saccharopine pathway promotes cancer metastasis through sumoylation of transcription machinery
item.description: The role of metabolism in metastasis remains unclear. Here, a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion and metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals a mechanism by which sumoylation driven by alpha-aminoadipate, the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase, drives metastasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: UNMASC: modelling non-monotonic dose responses to cytokine combinations
item.description: The authors present UNMASC, a model that captures non-monotonic cytokine combination effects. Applied to T cell development, UNMASC extends drug interaction surfaces to a broader range of dose-responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: A nanomolar-affinity antibody enabling sensitive labeling and high-resolution genomic mapping of O- GlcNAc
item.description: O‑GlcNAcylation is a widespread protein modification, but sensitive tools for its detection have been limited. Here, the authors develop a high‑affinity O‑GlcNAc antibody that enables detection, enrichment and genomic mapping of O‑GlcNAcylated proteins, revealing associations with active promoters and super‑enhancers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Podocyte-derived palmitic acid drives p53 S-palmitoylation and CD103 + CD4 + T cell differentiation in humanized mouse model of systemic lupus erythematosus
item.description: CD103 + CD4 + T cells mediate renal tissue injury in lupus nephritis (LN). To date, the mechanism instructing pathogenic CD103 + CD4 + T cell differentiation remains elusive. Here, the authors show that LN-associated podocytes undergo fatty acid oxidation reprogramming and release palmitic acid, thereby promoting p53 S-palmitoylation and Runx3 transcription in CD4⁺ T cells, ultimately sustaining pathogenic CD103⁺ T cell differentiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-ancestry genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association analyses identify new risk loci and genes for inflammatory bowel disease
item.description: Large-scale meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies and advanced transcriptome-wide association studies identify new inflammatory bowel disease risk variants and genes, including druggable targets with potential for therapeutic repurposing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gut microbiome of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder associates with clinical severity
item.description: Here, the authors show that gut microbes in children with autism vary with clinical severity, including reduced predicted GABAergic capacity, with sensory atypicalities showing the most associations, suggesting particular gut–brain relevance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mapping hippocampal subfield heterogeneity across neurological disorders by normative modeling
item.description: This study establishes age-specific reference ranges for hippocampal subfields and shows that personalized deviations from these norms can distinguish neurological disorders and help assess cognition and disease progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
item.description: Here authors introduce a comb‑shaped bioelectronic device that uses enhanced electric fields for electrostimulation and deep acid delivery for androgenetic alopecia treatment. In mouse models, they show that this safe, non‑invasive approach achieves nearly 100% hair regrowth within one month.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
item.description: Finger-specific motor control depends on neuromuscular compartments whose architecture has remained unresolved. Here, the authors combine dynamic ultrasound and MRI to map the compartments in 3D, reconstruct fibre level architecture, and validate them with anatomy and electromyography.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
item.description: Autoimmunity has long been hypothesized in schizophrenia spectrum disorders, but antibodies diagnostic of autoimmune encephalitis are uncommon. Here, the authors show that multi-platform profiling detects rare anti-neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins
item.description: Tuunanen et al. demonstrate a vasomechanic intervention to increase the efflux of soluble human brain proteins, including Aβ, into venous sinuses. The study shows how standard neuroimaging can monitor brain fluid dynamics during preventive efforts targeting proteinopathies such as Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis prevents pro-metastatic niche formation through metabolic rewiring of inflammatory monocytes
item.description: Targeting the IRE1α–XBP1s stress-sensor axis is widely viewed as a promising anti-tumor strategy. Here, the authors uncover an unexpected hepatocyte-specific role for this pathway in suppressing liver metastasis through metabolic regulation of inflammatory monocytes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
item.description: The study introduces a framework for measuring fairness in epidemic models. Tested across different epidemic scenarios, it shows that fairness-aware vaccination strategies can improve health equity and overall effectiveness.

item.title: Nature Communications: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
item.description: The authors sequence 1020 Chinese patients with beta thalassemia and 409 unaffected parents to identify genes that modulate the phenotypes. Functional validation in mice and cultured cells confirm the role of autophagy-associated gene PIK3C3.

item.title: Nature Communications: MELK drives neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis via vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic transition
item.description: The study identifies MELK as a driver of harmful vascular remodeling and shows that MELK inhibition reduces neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis in mice while preserving endothelial repair, highlighting MELK as a potential treatment target.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-anchored foundation model embeddings improve molecular prediction from histology images
item.description: Obtaining accurate molecular insights for precision oncology remains costly and time consuming. Here, the authors develop PathLUPI, a deep learning method to enable effective molecular prediction in cancer using only routine whole-slide images, with evaluation across 49 molecular oncology tasks in 20 different cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Culture-independent strain typing of Clostridioides difficile in fecal samples
item.description: Here, the authors optimize MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients, showcasing the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
item.description: Chronic kidney disease often causes heart enlargement, a serious complication whose mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that excess phosphate activates the metabolic enzyme GLS1, promoting heart enlargement, while blocking GLS1 protects against this effect in male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
item.description: Congenital lung anomalies are associated with Trisomy 21 lungs. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Shared genetic architecture across fibrotic diseases
item.description: The authors map the genetic architecture of 18 fibrosis-related conditions and find that fibrosis affecting anatomically distant parts shares genetic similarities, particularly in pathways involved in tissue remodeling, immune regulation and development.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reversal of trauma-induced monocyte paralysis by IFN-γ fails to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia, implicating lymphoid deficits in infection risk
item.description: The authors show that IFN-γ therapy improved monocyte HLA-DR expression in critically ill patients but failed to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia in the PREV-HAP trial. Pre-existing T- and B cell deficits, rather than monocyte status, predicted infection risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: One Health genomic surveillance identifies potential genetic links of antimicrobial-resistant foodborne pathogens across sectors
item.description: In this study, the authors use nationwide genomic data collected across sectors in Japan to identify closely related antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella and Campylobacter isolates in food and humans, highlighting the value of integrated One Health surveillance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Performance of artificial intelligence-assisted cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus testing for cervical cancer screening
item.description: The authors prove AI-assisted cytology effective for cervical cancer screening. When combined with HPV testing, it detects more precancerous lesions and maintains low referral rates.

item.title: Nature Communications: B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study
item.description: B7-H4 is a promising therapeutic target in solid tumors because of its frequent expression in cancer cells, limited normal tissue distribution, and immunosuppressive functions. In this first-in-human trial, the authors report safety and efficacy outcomes for B7-H4–directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with heavily pretreated ovarian, endometrial, and breast cancers, and cholangiocarcinoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Programmable hydrogel-nanocapsule protein delivery system targeting dense cartilage regeneration for osteoarthritis therapy
item.description: In osteoarthritis, protein therapeutics show poor joint retention and cartilage penetration. Here, authors develop a programmable two-stage, enzyme-responsive hydrogel-nanocapsule system to deliver a model protein drug and promote cartilage regeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Recruitment of TEX15 by HUSH2 drives repression of multicopy gene families in fertility regulation
item.description: In this study, Yang et al showed that the TEX15-HUSH2 complex represses multicopy gene families in haploid spermatids. Their study revealed a molecular mechanism underlying postmeiotic repression of sex chromatin (PMSC) critical for male fertility.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper
item.description: Golparian et al. designed and validated (13,701 global gonococcal genomes) SensiTyper, a rule-based framework predicting antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and susceptibility-guided individualized gonorrhoea treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tree shrew more closely recapitulates primate spermatogenesis than the mouse in cross-species single-cell transcriptomic analyses
item.description: By comparing testis cell development across four mammals, this study shows that tree shrews more closely resemble primates than mice in key stages of sperm formation, supporting their use as a complementary model of human male fertility.

item.title: Nature Communications: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics
item.description: This study finds that reasoning-enabled AI models improve diagnostic accuracy but produce more false positives and less consistent outputs but physician oversight helps retain benefits while reducing safety risks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Stabilization of insulin receptor mRNA by Star-PAP in metabolic homeostasis
item.description: Poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) are key regulators of mRNA stability. Star-PAP stabilizes insulin receptor mRNA to maintain adipose health and its loss causes lipodystrophy and insulin resistance, while pyruvate rescues the defects, highlighting RNA polyadenylation as a key to adipose homeostasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
item.description: Resistance selection in wastewater is poorly understood. In this study, the authors show that E. coli are selected for in Swedish hospital sewers, but not in municipal treatment plants and identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as drivers that enable targeted measures to manage risks for resistance evolution.

item.title: Nature Communications: Serine supplementation reinvigorates anti-tumor immunity by counteracting tumor cell SLC1A4-induced T cell starvation
item.description: Although serine restriction has been proposed as a strategy to limit tumor growth, its therapeutic utility remains uncertain and may compromise anti-tumor immunity. Here, the authors show that serine enhances CD8⁺ T cell function and that serine supplementation may help overcome resistance to PD-1 blockade.

item.title: Nature Communications: CADS: a comprehensive anatomical dataset and segmentation for whole-body anatomy in computed tomography
item.description: CADS brings together 22,022 diverse CT scans with annotations of 167 structures across the body. The openly available dataset and AI model enable large-scale whole-body anatomical analysis and perform robustly across public and hospital data.

item.title: Nature Communications: Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage
item.description: A study in Finnish and UK adults finds that deaths during extreme heat and cold are substantially higher among people with both pre-existing disease and socioeconomic disadvantage, identifying them as a priority for climate adaptation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Impression-R1 for radiological impression generation with multicenter benchmarking and prospective evaluations
item.description: Authors develop a domain-specific large reasoning model for radiological impression generation called Impression-R1. It generates diagnostic summaries from radiology findings and performed favorably across institutions and public datasets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Computational modeling and preclinical evaluation support targeting somatic instability for Huntington’s disease treatment
item.description: A one-time gene therapy targeting MSH3 reduced the expansion of HD-causing DNA repeats in preclinical studies. Patient-based modeling predicts this approach could delay symptom onset by years and meaningfully slow Huntington’s disease progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
item.description: This study presents a tailored erythropoietin fused to engineered albumin for extended plasma half-life after intravenous and subcutaneous delivery in mice. Following invasive or intranasal delivery, it promotes sustained erythrocyte proliferation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
item.description: Dengue is surging in temperate southern Brazil. This study links the rise to the spread and increasing infestation levels of Aedes aegypti, rather than to shifts in climate suitability, and shows that viral lineages persist locally for years.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes of enfortumab vedotin and NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer
item.description: The impact of sex-based differences on clinical outcomes of antibody-drug conjugates in patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) remains unclear. In here, the authors show that male patients have higher Nectin cell adhesion molecule 4 (NECTIN-4) expression as well as longer median overall survival and time on treatment while female patients experience higher rates of primary resistant disease despite similar baseline characteristics.

item.title: Nature Communications: NK cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor delay HIV rebound and reshape HIV reservoir composition
item.description: HIV persists during antiretroviral therapy in reservoirs that rapidly drive viral rebound when treatment stops. The authors here show that chimeric antigen receptor-engineered NK cells delay viral rebound and restrict rebound-associated viral lineages, leaving proviruses in less active chromatin.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
item.description: Fibro-inflammatory remodeling of visceral fat accompanies obesity and type 2 diabetes, but its drivers are poorly defined. Here, the authors show, using single-nucleus transcriptomics of human visceral adipose tissue, that THBS1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage TGFβ activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity
item.description: Vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching drives atherosclerosis and restenosis, but key regulators remain unclear. Here, the authors show DDIT4 promotes this switch via pyruvate dehydrogenase complex inhibition, reducing acetyl-CoA and histone acetylation, repressing contractile genes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Platelet-engineered AAV silencing of myocardial CD36 reprograms fatty acid metabolism to promote cardiac regeneration in male mice
item.description: Gene therapy for the injured heart is limited by poor targeting and neutralizing antibodies against viral vectors. Here, the authors show that platelets can ferry CD36-silencing AAV to damaged myocardium, reprogramming metabolism and restoring heart function in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior
item.description: Here the authors used long-term monitoring of 32 mother-child pairs to report that fetal day-night activity rhythms align with maternal circadian patterns, and that fetal sleep timing associates maternal sleep regularity and post-natal infant sleep patterns. These findings suggest that individual differences in sleep and circadian behavior may emerge before birth, although confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
item.description: The authors identified a major cluster of urothelial stem cells at the ureter-bladder junction. These cells efficiently formed colonies and organoids, and they renew ureteral urothelium and repair severe bladder urothelial injuries.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transient efferocytosis-induced activation of IKKβ reprograms macrophages to promote tissue resolution in mice
item.description: The clearance of apoptotic cells, or efferocytosis, reprograms macrophages towards a pro-resolving phenotype to facilitate tissue repair. Here, the authors identify IKKβ as an upstream regulator of immunoregulatory and reparative processes, showing that MerTK activation by apoptotic cells transiently activates an IKKβ-dependent NFKB/p38 axis, inducing IL-10 production, Rac1-mediated continuing efferocytosis, and activation of a Myc–TET2–PD-L1 pathway that promotes regulatory T cell expansion.

item.title: Nature Communications: One-shot synthesis of rare gastrointestinal lesions improves diagnostic accuracy and clinical training
item.description: Rare gastrointestinal lesions are seldom seen in endoscopy, limiting data for AI and clinician training. Here, authors present EndoRare, a one-shot retraining-free framework that synthesizes diverse lesion images from one reference to improve diagnosis and training.

item.title: Nature Communications: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
item.description: Noninvasive multitarget delivery to peri-infarct regions after ischemic stroke remains challenging. Here, authors use holographic focused ultrasound to deliver EVs and MSCs to infarct borders, promoting neurovascular repair in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
item.description: Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
item.description: Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features.

item.title: Nature Communications: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
item.description: Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
item.description: The authors developed a method to sequence Cryptosporidium directly from patient samples. They identified genetic differences among parasite populations, which provide new insight into how these parasites spread between humans and animals.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gut epithelial aryl hydrocarbon receptor deficiency aggravates fungal dysbiosis-mediated neutrophilic allergic airway disease in mice
item.description: Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma severity. Here the authors use mice deficient in intestinal epithelial cell AhR to show that in the absence of AhR, house dust mite-induced allergic airway disease is heightened in the presence of Candida albicans and fucosylation of lung structural cells affects neutrophil adhesion and retention in inflamed lung tissue involving inhibition of the mucus-utilising bacterium Akkermansia muciniphila .

item.title: Nature Communications: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy
item.description: Using human brain organoids, here authors report that GATOR1 loss impairs GABAergic interneurons via MAFB downregulation, independently of mTOR hyperactivation, offering new mechanistic insights into genetic focal epilepsy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort
item.description: A study of French Polynesians found hundreds of genetic variants that are common locally but rare worldwide and that alter metabolite levels and gene activity, including variants linked to lipid levels, type 2 diabetes and gout.

item.title: Nature Communications: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
item.description: This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.

item.title: Nature Communications: ZEB1 maintains energy metabolism to sustain cardiac function through synergistic regulation with TEAD1
item.description: Heart failure is a major health challenge, and the mechanisms driving metabolic dysfunction in the failing heart remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ZEB1-TEAD1 signaling preserves cardiac energy metabolism and that restoring ZEB1 or supplementing its downstream metabolite acetate mitigates heart failure progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Predicting follow-up cognition using estimated structural and functional connectivity networks and artificial intelligence in multiple sclerosis
item.description: Researchers used AI and clinically acquired MRI scans to estimate brain connectivity networks in people with multiple sclerosis, finding these estimates can moderately predict cognitive performance four years later and highlighting key brain circuits involved in cognition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Suppressor tRNAs restore functionally enhanced tumour suppressor protein to induce tumour regression
item.description: Nonsense mutations in tumour suppressor genes drive cancer initiation and progression but are thought to be “undruggable”. Here, the authors show that suppressor transfer RNAs can restore p53 from such mutations to induce tumour regression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression
item.description: In this study, authors show that serum metabolites measured before symptoms appear can predict which people with chronic Chagas disease will later develop heart damage, offering a way to identify patients at risk years in advance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular prosthetics for CFTR designed for anion selectivity outperform amphotericin B in cystic fibrosis airway epithelia
item.description: Here the authors design amphotericin B (AmB) to better mimic the missing CFTR ion channel in Cystic Fibrosis airway epithelia. These derivatives formed small molecule ion channels with increased permeability to anions and outperformed AmB.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fine-tuning of polygenic score to local data improves risk prediction and clinical implementation
item.description: A locally optimized framework that integrates multiple published polygenic risk scores substantially improves disease risk prediction over individual scores, providing a practical strategy for enhancing genetic risk assessment across diverse diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
item.description: This study used phylodynamic modelling of EV-D68 outbreak dynamics and found an association between clade B circulation and acute flaccid myelitis. However, this association weakened after COVID-19 emergence despite a resurgence of EV-D68 cases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extracorporeal photopheresis for the treatment of steroid-refractory immune related adverse events from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: a multi-center phase Ib/II clinical trial
item.description: Cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy develop immune-related adverse events. Here, the authors report the results of a multi-centre prospective phase Ib/II clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) therapy, showing ECP is a safe therapeutic option that could benefit the treatment of ICI-related inflammatory syndromes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
item.description: Gallstone disease is common, but its genetic basis remains incompletely understood. Here, the authors conduct a trans‑ancestry GWAS identifying 116 risk loci, linking gallstone susceptibility to lipid and liver metabolism pathways and expanding understanding of disease biology across diverse populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
item.description: Blood p-tau217 is a leading Alzheimer’s test but is also raised in ALS. Here, the authors show that muscle makes its own form of tau which leaks into the blood, and that detecting brain-derived p-tau217 improves the test’s accuracy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
item.description: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

item.title: Nature Communications: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming
item.description: Here, the authors show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O-antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae and that this surface-remodeling adaptation enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming.

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer
item.description: This study shows that tracking tumor DNA in blood can help predict outcomes, monitor treatment response, and reveal resistance in women receiving bireociclib plus fulvestrant for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
item.description: Authors developed a model of insecticide-treated net use that reflects current real-world conditions stratified by age and type. Results show growing adoption of next-generation nets, but overall coverage has stalled and use is declining.

item.title: Nature Communications: Low-valine diet ameliorates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by inhibiting LONP1-mediated degradation of ATP5F1B in male rodents
item.description: Restricting branched-chain amino acids is linked to metabolic benefits. Here, the authors show that valine directly binds ATP5F1B in cardiac tissue from hypertensive male rodents, and that low-valine diet stabilizes this protein by reducing LONP1-mediated degradation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic TFE3 activation in TFE3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder drives metabolic rigidity, lysosomal failure, and cell-extracellular matrix destabilization
item.description: This study reveals how persistent TFE3 activation triggers the neurodevelopmental disorder TFE3-NDD by disrupting critical cellular functions, including energy production, lysosomal function, and cell-matrix interactions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
item.description: Abnormal endogenous dsRNA generation and/or sensing and the resulting interferon responses contribute to immunotherapy resistance in microsatellitestable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC). Here, the authors identify the cytosolic tyrosine phosphatase PTPN12 as a central regulator that suppresses innate immune activation in MSS-CRC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study
item.description: Analysis of 1.35 million emergency department visits found that racial and ethnic disparities in triage scores were concentrated in lower-risk visits, where assessment relies more on clinical judgment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sevuparin in children with severe malaria: a phase I safety and dose-finding trial
item.description: This trial demonstrates the safety of sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive therapy in severe malaria in African children and identified, using a continual reassessment method design, the optimal dose to investigate in future trials.

item.title: Nature Communications: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
item.description: Genomic-based tests for Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. Here, the authors find that the multi-model transformer-based method HRDPath could be used as a digital biomarker to improve ovarian cancer diagnosis and therapy selection.’
